chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, and others, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from Abdul-A'la, the mawla of the family of Sam, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We are reported in our presence from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, hates the 'House of Meat'.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are lying! Rather, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The house in which people backbite one another and eat their brothers' flesh.' And my father (peace be upon him) was 'meat'-loving, and he passed away; and on the day he passed away, in the sleeve of the mother of his child, there were thirty dirhams for the meat.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'The House of Meat' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* corrects a common literalist misunderstanding of the phrase 'al-Bayt al-Lahm' by linking it to the idiom of 'eating the flesh' of others through backbiting (ghibah). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Prophet’s statement referred to the specific 'house' or context where this spiritual consumption occurred, rather than meat itself being disliked. The narration further grounds this teaching in the lived reality of the Ahl al-Bayt, noting that Imam Ali (AS) himself enjoyed meat and died with funds reserved for it, thereby refuting the notion of ascetic rejection of meat.
